<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via ToolExecutionContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via ToolExecutionContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v9.mdx`  _(via ToolExecutionContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 355c73c7ede0363a045049ddc34e91ebd9a6e856` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fab76e3b09f5fa89805426174e93c5a4c6702e41` — the merge of head `47d6faf20ec22a689f5d1709a00d412a01f90c98` into base `355c73c7ede0363a045049ddc34e91ebd9a6e856`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fab76e3b09f5fa89805426174e93c5a4c6702e41 && git checkout fab76e3b09f5fa89805426174e93c5a4c6702e41
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 355c73c7ede0363a045049ddc34e91ebd9a6e856 47d6faf20ec22a689f5d1709a00d412a01f90c98 && git checkout -B drift-repro 355c73c7ede0363a045049ddc34e91ebd9a6e856 && git merge --no-ff 47d6faf20ec22a689f5d1709a00d412a01f90c98

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 355c73c7ede0363a045049ddc34e91ebd9a6e856
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 355c73c7ede0363a045049ddc34e91ebd9a6e856` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `da20d2d10bca3e4432fc57774f854d0c27cb02e0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/chatFocus.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatFocusRow.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/ChatDockConversation.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAgents.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37123 for card #36999, net diff against `main` (merge base `254e396a`), 26 files. Inputs read: the card body and its three comments (triage, claim, os-dev-report), topic #36996's rulings, the PR body and file list, the diff, and the check-runs on this head. No `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `.claude/**`. `Security-touching: yes` because the `focus` docblock teaches access behaviour (advisory, never an access decision, re-read as the caller); the path is not a skill, so no label follows from it.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ToolExecutionContext.focus?: { object: string; id: string }[]` (ai-service.ts) — an optional member added to a context interface beside `surfaceContext`. Accept-set widening only: every existing producer and consumer of the interface still type-checks. Shape, name, array form and docblock match the card's item 1 and the topic ruling (per conversation, one record in phase 1, client-reported, advisory, never an access decision). Right.
- `AiAgentCapabilitiesSchema.focus: z.boolean().optional()` (protocol.zod.ts) — a response-side key on the `GET /api/v1/ai/agents` row. Optional, so every row served today still parses and the inferred output type only gains `focus?: boolean`; a non-boolean is refused. The card's item 4 asks for "one flag on the discovery the console already reads, named in the PR"; the agents catalog is that discovery (`useAgents`) and the PR names the flag. Right as a schema change. It IS a public-surface addition the ratchet records: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/AiAgentCapabilities:focus`. The PR declares that as no metadata-protocol change, which is wrong (see ②, M1).
- `AiAgentChatRequestSchema.context` stays `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`: `context.focus` passes the declared request shape with no schema change. Right.
- First reader (topic ruling, ADR-0049): `capabilities.focus` lands with its reader in this PR (`normalizeCapabilities`, `agentHasCapability`, `ChatPane.focusHonoured`). `ToolExecutionContext.focus` lands with its sender only; its server reader is the cloud child (topic row 9), a split the maintainer-filed card states in its own Out of scope, and the key is a request-context field rather than authorable metadata (`Spec property liveness` is green on this head). Right, on the card's authority.
- `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`: exported `AgentCapabilities` gains a required `focus: boolean`; `agentHasCapability`'s name fallback is narrowed to the four build-era capabilities, so the four existing answers are unchanged and `focus` is never inferred from a name. No other construction site of an `AgentCapabilities` literal exists outside tests in the tree at this head. Right.
- `@object-ui/app-shell`: new root exports `setChatFocus` and `ChatFocus`; `ChatPane` gains optional `conversationFocus`. Additions only. With no flag `promptHeaderSlot`, `surfaceContextLabel` and `surfaceContextTitle` receive exactly the values they received before (`composerContextRow` reduces to `pendingDraftsBar ?? undefined`; `focusRow` is null) and `buildFocusContext` spreads nothing. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — the PR body and the changeset both carry it, with no direction arm; correct for an additive change (nothing removed, renamed or narrowed).

M1 (must-fix) — the metadata-protocol declaration and the level are wrong, and the gate says so: `Check Changeset` concluded FAILURE on this head. The PR body and `.changeset/36999-conversation-focus.md` declare `Metadata-protocol: none` and grade `@objectstack/spec` `patch`, while the diff moves a metadata-protocol baseline the ratchet records (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, +`api/AiAgentCapabilities:focus`). By the rule the gate enforces (maintainer ruling A, 2026-10-21, on #25105) a key that enters is `Metadata-protocol: added`, and the package carrying it is graded at least `minor`. Fix: declare `Metadata-protocol: added` on the PR body and in the changeset, and grade `@objectstack/spec` at least `minor` (read the gate's "WHICH LEVEL" text for whether the three `@object-ui/*` entries move with it). The baseline is not to be edited to quiet the gate. This is a changeset edit, so the head moves and the fix earns a delta review.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head when read: `Check Changeset` FAILURE (M1). Success: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, filter, both shard planners. Still running and not awaited: Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check (debt ledger, workspace, source gates, consumer gates), Lint (ESLint, docs and code guards, PM dispatch-gates, repo and tooling gates, CI release and engine gates, and the three scoped lint jobs). No verdict in this record rests on a run that has not concluded; the tests the dev reports are the dev's local readings, not gate verdicts.
- Open question (chip inside the input frame, A, or the in-flow row, B): answered, not escalated. The card already rules the place: item 3 names "the composer slot that draws the page chip today". B as shipped is therefore a recorded deviation, acceptable on this head only because no server declares `capabilities.focus` and, flag off, the chip stays exactly where it was. A is the answer: file the follow-up card on `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` (a node slot for the chip in `ChatbotEnhanced`) and order it before the cloud child that serves `focus: true`, since from that moment the page chip of EVERY page, record or not, leaves the input's top edge (the #35445 placement). No maintainer decision is needed; the card's text decides it.
- Dev deviation, file surface: `protocol.zod.ts`, `useAgents.ts`, the two new app-shell files and the root export are the flag's declaration, its reader and the setter the card itself asks for; `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` was left alone per stop-on-breach. Accepted.
- Dev deviation, affected UI suites read at `ac2c078b` rather than at this head: the CI test shards on this head are the verdict and are still running (listed above).
- Out-of-scope note (the exported `AiChatPage` is no longer routed): observation only; it does not bear on the contract.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The only new read is one `findOne(object, id)` per chip (the pinned record, plus the offered record while the offer shows), made in the browser as the user. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts** — holds against the card and the topic ruling. Checked sentence by sentence against the sender: "on every turn" (`body.context` is read per send and spreads `buildFocusContext`); "does not follow navigation" (state is keyed on the conversation id, not the route); "at most one entry" (`buildFocusContext` emits a one-element array); "the request body is the authority; whatever a host stores only restores its display" (the client stores per tab and re-sends from its own state; nothing server-stored is read back); "a client sends it only to an agent whose catalog row declares `capabilities.focus: true`" (`focusHonoured`). The naming note (`scope` is the conversation cache key) is true of `useChatConversation.ts` in the live tree. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts** — the flag sits on the right object (the per-agent `capabilities` precedent), is optional, and its description agrees with the contract docblock and with its reader. Design holds; its declaration is M1.

**ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAgents.ts** — agrees with the contract: `focus` is true only on `raw.focus === true`; with a declared `capabilities` object the declaration answers; with none, `focus` is false for every name, build agents included. While the catalog is still loading the answer is false, so neither chip nor key appears; consistent. No finding.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/chatFocus.ts**

S1 (should-fix) — the first-send carry fires on every `undefined` to id transition, not only on a mint. `useConversationFocus` treats `state.key === undefined && conversationId !== undefined && state.entry.focus !== null` as "the first send minted this id". In both hosts `paneConversationId` also goes from `undefined` to an EXISTING id without any send: `useChatConversation` starts at `undefined` and resolves the resumed thread asynchronously, a fresh ("New conversation") target has no id until its first send, and `scopeMatched` blanks the id between apps. So: pin record A on a not-yet-sent conversation, then open conversation X from the history (or move to an app whose thread resumes) and X receives A: X's own stored focus is never read, the effect overwrites X's stored entry with A, and X's next turns send `focus: [A]`. That contradicts the ruling "focus is per conversation" and this module's own sentence "Moving to another conversation restores that one's chip from storage". The chip is visible and the value advisory, hence should-fix and not must-fix. A fix has to tell a mint apart from a resume (for example, carry only onto an id the host's `ensureConversation` returned) while keeping the deliberate `setChatFocus` hand-off ("pin, then open the drawer") landing on the thread the drawer resolves; add the test (pin on an unsent conversation, open an existing one, expect its own focus or none).

Otherwise the module agrees with the contract: the render-time carry gives the remounted pane the focus before its replay; a new conversation starts unpinned; storage is per tab and never sent; the module imports no chat code.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx** (`ChatPane`) — one builder for page and dock; the key is absent, not empty, without a pin or without the flag; flag off, the composer props are value-identical to `main`. A `ChatFocusRow` that renders nothing leaves no gap (`empty:hidden` on the slot wrapper in `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`, read in the tree). No finding beyond the placement answered in ③.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatFocusRow.tsx** — the pin is offered only when the surface names one record (`artifact.type === 'object'` with `selection.kind === 'record'`, the shape `consoleChatSurface` builds for record pages and the list drawer); the name is read as the user and an unreadable record keeps its pair; the offer shows only for a different record and not after a decline; a new pin resets the decline. Agrees with the card's item 3 and the PR's stated reading of "remembered for the conversation".
- nit — the switch offer falls back to the bare record id when the name cannot be read, where the pinned chip falls back to the `object · id` pair.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/ChatDockConversation.tsx** — the focus is held above the keyed pane and keyed on `paneConversationId`; nothing in the thread scope or the dock target reads it, so the focus never re-keys the thread. Agrees. Exposed to S1 through the hook.
- nit — `setChatFocus` on a host whose agent does not declare the flag still records the focus in state and `sessionStorage`; nothing is drawn or sent, so "no flag, nothing changes" holds for the user and the request.

Open on this head: M1, S1.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36999-conversation-focus`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZrXaP3ZXVbM6u2b7S`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f7987f47ec6c811ae6f0d2c8131584dcccb26db`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/chatFocus.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatFocusRow.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/ChatDockConversation.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAgents.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta review of PR #37123 for card #36999: `da20d2d1..5f7987f4` (three commits, six files: the changeset, `chatFocus.ts`, `AiChatPage.tsx`, `ChatDockConversation.tsx`, `ChatFocusRow.tsx`, the focus test), judged against M1 and S1 of the record on `da20d2d1`. The two `hits` files and `useAgents.ts` are byte-identical to the head already reviewed, so that record's ① and its ④ on those three files stand. Inputs re-read: the PR body as it now stands, the card thread (it carries no os-dev-report newer than comment 7143839494, so the delta is judged from the tree and the PR body alone), the delta, and the check-runs on this head. `Security-touching: yes` for the same reason as before (the `focus` docblock teaches access behaviour); no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `.claude/**`.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set or published-schema change in the delta: `packages/spec/**` and `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/**` are untouched since `da20d2d1`. The earlier judgments stand, each right.
- `ConversationFocus` (the object a chat host hands `ChatPane`, internal to app-shell and not exported from the package root) gains `markSending`; the host registered with `setChatFocus` is now the hook's `handOff` instead of `setFocus`. The root exports (`setChatFocus`, `ChatFocus`) are unchanged in name and signature. Right.
- Both hosts now pass `ChatPane` a wrapper of `ensureConversation` that marks the send first and returns the same promise. `ensureConversation` is called only where the pane has no conversation id (`useDeferredFirstSend`, read in the tree), so a send on an existing conversation marks nothing. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — unchanged on the PR body and the changeset, no direction arm; correct for an additive change.

M1: closed. The changeset and the PR body now declare `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` is graded `minor`, the three `@object-ui/*` entries stay `patch`, and no baseline was edited in the delta. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head when read: every concluded gate is success, among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, all Type Check and Lint jobs, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16 and Test Core 2 to 8 and 10 of 10. One earlier `PR-body guards` run shows cancelled beside the successful one (superseded by the body edit). Still running and not awaited: Test Core (1/10) and Test Core (9/10).
- Open question (chip placement): answered in the previous record, unchanged by the delta: A, as a follow-up card on `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` ordered before the cloud child that serves `focus: true`; no escalation.
- The dev posted no new report on the card for this head; nothing new is flagged there to answer.
- SQL push-down: the delta adds no read. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts**, **packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts**, **ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAgents.ts** — unchanged; the previous judgment stands with no finding.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/chatFocus.ts**

S1: still open, narrowed. The sequence S1 named is fixed and pinned by a test: a focus pinned with the chip on an unsent conversation no longer follows the user into a history row, a resumed thread or another app's thread (`carry` false, no mark, so the arriving conversation's stored focus is read and stays intact). Two quick sends and a send that lands while a resumed thread is still resolving both behave correctly (the mark is idempotent and the id that arrives is the one the send goes to). What remains is the same defect through a mark that is never spent:

- S1 (should-fix), path one — a first send whose create fails. `markSending` sets `sendingRef` and only the effect on a defined `key` clears it. When `ensureConversation` settles with no id (the create fails and the host shows `createError`, or there is no user) the mark stays set while the host still has no id. The next id to arrive of any kind, for example a history row opened after the failed send, then takes the pinned focus and overwrites that conversation's stored entry.
- S1 (should-fix), path two — a hand-off that no id ever spends. `handOff` sets `carry` whenever the host has no id, and `carry` is cleared only when an id arrives. On a host that has settled with nothing to resume (a fresh conversation), `carry` stays set indefinitely, and `setFocus` and `decline` preserve it. So after one `setChatFocus` call on such a host, a later chip pin of another record followed by a history open carries that record onto the opened conversation: the original S1 sequence again. This contradicts the module's own sentence that a history row "reads that conversation's own stored focus instead".

Both need an unusual sequence and the value is advisory with a visible chip, so should-fix, not must-fix. A fix spends the mark when the create settles without an id, and drops `carry` once the focus is changed through the chip or the host's resolve settles with no thread; add a test per path.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx**, **ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/ChatDockConversation.tsx** — the wrappers agree with the hook's contract ("the host calls this beside `ensureConversation`"), return the original promise unchanged, and mark in a ref, so the pane holding the first message is not re-rendered by the mark. No new finding; exposed to S1 path one through the hook.

**ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatFocusRow.tsx** — the switch offer now falls back to the `object · id` pair, as the pinned chip does; the earlier nit is fixed and the test pins the new text.
- nit (carried, accepted deviation) — `setChatFocus` on a host whose agent does not declare the flag still records the focus in state and `sessionStorage`; nothing is drawn or sent.

No must-fix on this head. Open on this head: S1.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36999-conversation-focus`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZrXaP3ZXVbM6u2b7S`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f7d9cc141a1d9f5b083fc471490f4ea0125d7190`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/chatFocus.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatFocusRow.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/ChatDockConversation.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAgents.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Second delta review of PR #37123 for card #36999: `5f7987f4..f7d9cc14` (one commit, four files: `chatFocus.ts`, `AiChatPage.tsx`, `ChatDockConversation.tsx`, the focus test), judged against the two S1 paths left open by the record on `5f7987f4`. The two `hits` files, `useAgents.ts`, `ChatFocusRow.tsx` and the changeset are byte-identical to heads already reviewed, so the earlier ①, ② and the ④ judgments on those files stand. Inputs re-read: the PR body, the card thread including os-dev-report comment 7146307286, the delta, and the check-runs on this head. `Security-touching: yes` for the same reason as before (the `focus` docblock teaches access behaviour); no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `.claude/**`.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set or published-schema change in the delta: `packages/spec/**` and `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/**` are untouched. The earlier judgments stand, each right.
- `useConversationFocus` gains an optional second parameter, the host's `createError`. The hook is internal to app-shell (not exported from the package root); both hosts pass it. Root exports unchanged. Right.
- Both hosts name the user they hand `useChatConversation` (`conversationUserId`) and pass the hook the same expression as before, so the conversation's resolution is value-identical; the send wrapper marks only while that user exists. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — unchanged on the PR body and the changeset, no direction arm; correct for an additive change.

M1: closed (on `5f7987f4`; nothing in this delta touches the changeset or the declaration). `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head: `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` minor, the three `@object-ui/*` entries patch.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head when read: every concluded gate is success, among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, all Type Check and Lint jobs, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16 and Test Core 1 to 8 and 10 of 10. Still running and not awaited: Test Core (9/10).
- Open question (chip placement), accepted deviation by maintainer ruling. The seat relays that the maintainer ruled on it on 2026-11-24 21:54Z: 「先这样上线，也不立卡，我先看效果再说」. - Path one (a first send that mints nothing). The mark is now spent when the host's `createError` arrives, and is not set at all without a user. The dev's choice not to clear on every no-id return of `ensureConversation` is right: read in `useChatConversation.ts`, a no-id return with a user is one of three things. A create that failed sets `createError` (a new error object per failure, so the effect fires each time). A resolve that could not read the thread, with this send recorded, also sets `createError`. A send recorded while the host is still resolving returns no id and no error, and is then either fulfilled by the settle (a create, whose failure reports as above) or joins the thread the resolve found; in both the id that arrives is the one the held message is replayed into, so keeping the mark is correct there and clearing it would drop the focus from a turn that is really sent. A retry after a failure marks again after the effect has run, and the error is cleared before the new create, so the retry's minted id still takes the focus. No path was found on which a marked send with a user ends with neither an id nor a `createError`.
- Path two (a hand-off's carry outliving its own focus). A chip pin of another record, a remove, and a decline now drop `carry`; a hand-off of `null` carries nothing (a carry needs a focus).
